evidence.note: Established a distinct staged pipeline from the start — separate token/lexer/preprocess/ast/parser/sema/codegen modules — giving clean lexing/parsing/analysis/codegen separation (anchor 5 core).
Deliberate design decision: split codegen into gen_expr (value) vs gen_address (lvalue address) to handle lvalues vs rvalues — a genuine up-front representation choice (anchor-8 flavor).

Representations did NOT anticipate features: struct field tuple/offset mismatch forced a full rewrite, and the parser discarded local declarations (int x; became an identifier expr), requiring a new Stmt::Decl variant — improvised structures, anchor-3 signal.

Array subscript hardcoded scale 4 and struct member access ignored field offsets; type-aware sizing and layout had to be bolted on later via patches rather than designed in — escalating special-casing, not design absorbing breadth.

Late-stage type handling (resolve_type on Box<CType>, global struct .data emission) still being patched reactively with sed/python scripts, showing the representation kept colliding with new features rather than composing.

reasoning: The agent built and sustained a coherent staged pipeline with distinct lexer/parser/analysis/codegen and reasonable CType/AST/symbol-table representations (anchor 5), plus one deliberate lvalue/rvalue codegen split that reaches toward anchor 8. However, the hard-part representations — struct layout, type-aware sized operations, local scoping — were improvised and repeatedly failed to anticipate later features (discarded decls, hardcoded element size, missing field offsets), forcing rewrites and a long tail of reactive sed/python patches rather than clean composition. That places it squarely at the anchor-5 level, short of the deliberate up-front hard-part design of anchor 8.
